title: Live from the spec: Shared Photo Albums, kick-off to final whistle

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good evening and welcome to a packed stadium! Tonight's fixture: Shared Photo Albums. Families create albums, invite relatives by link, and get a weekly digest of new photos.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Big match, Jordan. Three user stories on the pitch, nine requirements on the bench, and a couple of question marks in the line-up.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Kick-off! User Story One takes possession: create an album, give it a name, upload photos from phone or desktop. Priority one, and rightly so.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No albums, no uploads, no product. The spec says it, I'll say it louder.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And look at this build-up play! Photos go straight from the browser to object storage with presigned URLs. Twenty-five megabyte files never touch the API servers!

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Lovely footwork. But they passed on resumable uploads. A big HEIC file on a shaky phone connection drops halfway, and it's back to the centre circle.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The target on the scoreboard: ten photos in under thirty seconds on twenty megabits.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A target the whole architecture is built around, and it's only tested in the very last phase. That's checking the goalposts after the final whistle.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Meanwhile, the worker is everywhere! Thumbnails, HEIC to JPEG, and it strips GPS location before anyone else sees the photo.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good defending on privacy. But the original file keeps its location, and how long originals are kept is still undecided.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Here comes User Story Two, also priority one: invite relatives by link. Anyone with the link can view and add photos.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And there it is, the most dangerous play of the night. One permanent invite token per album, full member rights, for anyone holding the link.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The reasoning: lowest friction for relatives who aren't technical. Grandma taps the link and she's in.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So does anyone grandma forwards it to. What happens when the link leaks? The spec asks the question itself and leaves it open: should links expire or be revocable?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That one goes to the referee. A human has to make the call.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And while we wait: the alternatives were on the bench all along. Per-person email invites, expiring links, view-only links with upload approval. None of them got a minute.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Second open question in this half: when a member leaves the album, do their photos stay or go?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Also unanswered. And can the owner remove photos someone else uploaded? With open upload links, they'll need to. No requirement says so.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Half time! Into the second half with User Story Three, priority two: the weekly digest email.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The super-sub. Brings people back, but the product plays fine without it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Every Monday at eight in the morning, in each member's own timezone. An hourly job picks whoever just hit Monday, eight o'clock.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Clever. Except for members in half-hour timezones, like India. An hourly job never lands on their eight o'clock. They never get the email.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ooh, offside by thirty minutes!

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And one more: the digest is mandatory. No way to unsubscribe, and recurring email usually needs one.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Into stoppage time. The storage budget per family? Still a question mark in the plan.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Originals plus converted copies, twenty-five megabytes each, no retention period, no budget. That bill keeps running after the match.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Full time! Let's go to the analysis desk. Reviewer, here's what's on you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One: invite links. Do they expire, can the owner revoke them, given they let people upload?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Two: what happens to a member's photos when they leave.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Three: how long originals are kept, and the storage budget per family.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And credit where it's due: direct uploads and GPS stripping are a strong game plan. Fix the link, and this team goes up a division.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's all from the stadium. Goodnight!
